- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.0) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% for next 3–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 2–4 days.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in the 2nd half of the 30-day window.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.5) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth; add 1–3% noise to forecast for 3–5 days to capture short-term spikes.
